SELF_MANAGE.label: You can do this at home
SELF_MANAGE.detail: If it's worse tomorrow, or it hasn't settled in a few days, ring your GP.

PHARMACIST.label: Your pharmacist can help with this today
PHARMACIST.detail: No appointment. Talking to them costs nothing, and many are open late.

GP_NEXT.label: This one's for your GP, and it can wait
GP_NEXT.detail: We've written it down for you — it's in your list below. Take it to your next visit.

GP_NOW.label: Call your GP today
GP_NOW.detail: Call your practice and tell them it's a flare. If they can't fit you in, call healthdirect on 1800 022 222 — a nurse answers, any hour.
GP_NOW.callLabel: Call healthdirect — a nurse, any hour

ED.label: Get seen tonight
ED.detail: Don't wait for a GP appointment. If you can't get to an emergency department, or you're not sure, call healthdirect now and a nurse will tell you what to do. If you are very unwell, call 000.

t-septic.ask: Is a joint hot, red or swollen — and you also feel feverish, shivery, or generally unwell?

t-cauda.ask: Any new numbness around your groin or between your legs, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowel?

t-rash.ask: Any new rash, blisters, or ulcers in your mouth since starting a new medicine?

t-gca.ask: Are you over 50 with a new headache at your temple or scalp, aching in your jaw when you chew, or any change to your vision?

septic-joint.catches: A hot, swollen joint together with fever or feeling generally unwell
septic-joint.why: An infected joint (septic arthritis) looks almost exactly like a gout or arthritis flare — hot, red, swollen, agonising. The difference is that an infected joint destroys itself within days and can make you dangerously unwell. It cannot be told apart from a flare without testing the fluid in the joint.

cauda-equina.catches: Back pain with numbness in the saddle area, or loss of bladder or bowel control, or new weakness in both legs
cauda-equina.why: These are signs the nerves at the base of the spine are being compressed. It is one of the few genuine emergencies in back pain, and the damage becomes permanent within hours. Everything else about back pain can wait. This cannot.

allopurinol-rash.catches: A new rash, blisters or mouth ulcers after starting allopurinol
allopurinol-rash.why: Allopurinol can rarely trigger a severe allergic skin reaction. Caught early it is survivable; ignored for a few days it can be fatal. Any new rash after starting allopurinol is treated as that reaction until proven otherwise — stop the drug and be seen the same day.

gi-bleed.catches: Black or tarry stools, or vomiting blood, while taking anti-inflammatories
gi-bleed.why: Anti-inflammatories can cause bleeding in the stomach. Black tarry stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds mean it is already bleeding. This is an emergency regardless of how well you otherwise feel.

chest-breathing.why: Neither belongs to your musculoskeletal condition and both can be immediately life-threatening. This is not something to work out at home.

trauma.catches: Unable to put weight on it after a fall or injury, or the joint looks deformed
trauma.why: That pattern suggests a fracture or dislocation rather than a flare, and it needs an X-ray.

giant-cell-arteritis.catches: A new headache at the temple, jaw ache when chewing, scalp tenderness, or any change to vision — especially over 50
giant-cell-arteritis.why: In people over 50 these can be giant cell arteritis — inflammation of the arteries at the temple. Untreated it can cause sudden and permanent loss of vision within days, so it is treated as an emergency. A change to your vision in particular cannot wait.
